stories.title: Benefits and risks of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators in children and young adults with congenital heart disease, primary electrical disease or paediatric cardiomyopathy†.
stories.description: This study focuses on evaluating the benefits and risks of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) in pediatric and congenital heart disease (CHD) patients from 2001 to 2023. Among 214 patients (61% with CHD), 41% received appropriate ICD therapy, particularly those with secondary prevention indications, while 13% experienced inappropriate shocks and 36% required unplanned surgeries, mainly due to lead-related complications and abdominal generator placement. The use of epicardial/extracardiac leads and abdominal generator location were identified as significant risk factors for unplanned surgeries. Subcutaneous ICDs (sICDs) showed a trend toward fewer complications but with limited sample size. The findings highlight the importance of individualized risk assessment, device selection, and programming to optimize ICD therapy and reduce complications in this population.

stories.title: "It's not just some cookie cutter that you have to fit into": A qualitative study of immigrant women and girls' needs, experiences, and barriers to sexual and reproductive health education in Canada.
stories.description: This article focuses on the experiences and needs of immigrant women and girls in Canada regarding sexual and reproductive health (SRH) education. Through three focus group discussions with ten immigrant women across Canada, the study identified key barriers such as language difficulties, cultural stigma, and a Western-centric, heteronormative curriculum that often excludes diverse cultural and LGBTQ+ perspectives. Participants reported seeking alternative SRH information outside formal education due to these gaps and emphasized the importance of inclusive, culturally sensitive curricula delivered by diverse educators in safe, accessible spaces. The findings suggest that provincial Ministers of Education should use these insights to develop more comprehensive and intersectional SRH educational programs that better serve Canada's diverse immigrant populations.

stories.title: Efficacy of Ultrasound-Guided Renal Access for Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy in Combination with Fluoroscopy versus Fluoroscopy as a Single Imaging Modality.
stories.description: The article focuses on multiple clinical studies conducted at Ain Shams University Hospitals addressing urological conditions and treatments. One study compared flexible ureteroscopy (FURS) with and without the use of a ureteral access sheath (UAS) in patients with upper ureteric stones, finding no significant differences in complications or stone-free rates but a longer operative time with UAS. Another trial evaluated submucosal intravesical injections of autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) for interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) resistant to conventional treatments, reporting a 63.3% success rate and significant symptom improvement. Additionally, a study on percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) compared combined ultrasound and fluoroscopy guidance versus fluoroscopy alone, showing reduced radiation exposure and shorter hospital stays with combined guidance but no significant difference in overall outcomes. Lastly, a randomized trial assessed the efficacy of tamsulosin plus tadalafil versus tamsulosin alone for lower ureteric stones, demonstrating faster stone expulsion and fewer colic episodes with the combination therapy. These findings contribute to optimizing urological interventions with attention to safety, efficacy, and patient outcomes.

stories.title: A wicked problem: The rising tide of pollution at Ilavalai Beach, Sri Lanka.
stories.description: This article examines a practice-led research project by ArtsAction Group (AAG) involving socially engaged art (SEA) and science, technology, engineering, art, and math (STEAM) workshops with Tamil secondary students in Ilavalai, Sri Lanka, focused on the community challenge of ocean and beach pollution. The project integrates the engineering design process (EDP) with SEA to engage students in researching, prototyping, and reflecting on solutions to this "wicked problem," while fostering capacities for hope, resilience, and future-making as cultural practices. Set against a backdrop of post-war trauma, cultural erasure, and ongoing social challenges faced by the Tamil community, the workshops emphasize collaborative, student-centered learning and the role of arts and culture in social transformation and community empowerment. The article highlights the importance of relational, ethical partnerships grounded in respect and loving kindness, while acknowledging that such educational initiatives alone cannot resolve systemic environmental injustices.

stories.title: Prediction of seismic response of building structures using a CNN-LSTM-ATT network with transfer learning.
stories.description: This article focuses on the development and validation of a convolutional long short-term memory neural network with attention mechanism (CNN-LSTM-ATT) for predicting the nonlinear seismic response of building structures. The model integrates convolutional neural networks (CNN) for local feature extraction, long short-term memory networks (LSTM) for temporal sequence modeling, and attention mechanisms (ATT) to enhance focus on critical input features. Through ablation studies and transfer learning strategies—fine-tuning pre-trained models based on finite element simulations with limited real structural data—the CNN-LSTM-ATT demonstrated superior accuracy in predicting seismic responses of both numerical models and actual structures compared to traditional finite element models and other deep learning variants. The study highlights the model's potential for rapid and reliable seismic response prediction across various structural types, while noting limitations related to reliance on numerical pre-training and the need for some target-domain data for fine-tuning.
